newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says economy must pick up to hit 2.5 pct goal.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says economy must pick up to hit 2.5 pct goal.

text.p: German economic growth must accelerate if it is to hit the government's 2.5 percent forecast for the full year and conditions for this remain good, the economics ministry said in its monthly report.
The 1.4 percent annual growth reported last week for the first quarter understated the expansion by more than one full percentage point due to three fewer workdays in the quarter, it said.

"To achieve the expected 2.5 percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP) for this year, a further acceleration of the current growth tempo is needed," the report said. "The conditions for this remain favourable."
Exports remain the main engine of growth, spurred by correction of the mark and vigorous economies in other countries, it said.
This helped to fuel a steep rise in industrial orders through April, and that month's disappointing production figures are likely to be revised upward, it said.

The labour market continues to show little improvement, it said. But the May rise in seasonally adjusted unemployment was largely due to lower government intervention, not economic sluggishness, it said.
